Let mu(Y)=1-(1-p(Y))^n (OR over n equal independent channels; Y=g/s, s=c*sqrt(G rho_Lambda)=2*a0 on the adopted kappa=1/2 footing), p a completion with p(0)=0, p'(0)=1, p(inf)=1. (A) Certified identity: (d/dY)[1-(1-pY)^n]|_0 = n*(1-p(0))^(n-1)*p'(0) = n for every such p (Lean, axioms {propext,Classical.choice,Quot.sound}, zero sorry). (B) CDF axioms do not fix the slope: the corpus family {mu_m(Y)=1-(1+Y)^(-m): m in N} is CDF-shaped with slope m at 0 for every m (slopes 1 and 2 certified), so kappa = a0/s = 1/n is carried by the physical premises (OR semantics, p'(0)=1, channel count n), not by the probability reading. (C) Counterexample (capable of failing, passed): measures A (one global uniform: xi(Y)=1{U<=p(Y)}), B (per-Y i.i.d. Bernoulli), C_lambda (block-correlated, lambda=1/2,1,2) have IDENTICAL marginals - hence identical expectations mu(Y) and identical quasi-linear operators div(mu(|grad Phi|/s) grad Phi)=4pi G rho_b - yet pairwise-different fluctuation spectra (Cov_A(Y1,Y2)=min(p1,p2)-p1*p2 > 0 vs Cov_B=0 for Y1!=Y2; e.g. at (0.25,0.75): 0.114286 vs 0; at (0.75,1.25): 0.190476 vs 0; C_lambda interpolates). (D) Deep-limit transfer g^2=(s/n)g_N = a0 g_N is asymptotic, not exact: Y*/Y_dm = 1 + ((n+1)/4)Y_dm + ((n+1)(7n-1)/96)Y_dm^2 + ... with quantified finite-D residuals (rel in [5.0e-3,6.1e-2] for D=1e-4..1e-2, n=1..3); Newtonian deficit 1-mu = Y^(-n) - n Y^(-n-1) + O(n(n+1)/2 Y^(-n-2)). (E) Testable consequence beyond the CDF: if the response were an N-cell stochastic realization, sigma_g/g_N = sqrt(mu(1-mu)/N)/mu^2 (0.7698/0.2434/7.70e-3 at n=2, Y=1, N=1/10/1e4) vs EXACTLY 0 for the deterministic response - the fluctuation spectrum, not the CDF, is observably discriminable. Conclusion: the probability/CDF reading does not specify the gravitational response; the sample space and the joint law of the channel process are free data; the exact missing equation is the finite-dimensional joint law (covariance kernel/generator) of the channel process. kappa=1/2 remains an ADOPTED input (consistent with k01 outcome 3).
